1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Anaphylaxis is a severe, life-threatening systemic allergic reaction that affects over 15 million Americans,
with an incidence rate of 2.1 per 1,000 person-years. Despite being preventable with early epinephrine
administration, mortality from anaphylaxis remains significant due to delayed recognition and treatment.
This project proposes an Intelligent Physiological Pattern-Based System — a wearable IoT device
integrated with machine learning algorithms that continuously monitors multi-modal physiological signals
to detect anaphylaxis in its earliest stages and automatically trigger emergency interventions including
epinephrine auto-injection, caregiver alerts, and emergency service notification.
Key Innovation: The system leverages physiological pattern recognition (heart rate variability, skin
conductance, temperature fluctuations, and respiratory patterns) rather than relying solely on visible
symptoms, enabling detection before clinical symptoms become apparent to the patient or observer.
2. PROBLEM CONDITION AND OCCURRENCE
2.1 What is Anaphylaxis?
Anaphylaxis is a rapid-onset, potentially fatal systemic allergic reaction occurring within minutes to hours
of allergen exposure. It involves the release of inflammatory mediators (histamine, tryptase, leukotrienes,
prostaglandins) from mast cells and basophils, causing widespread vasodilation, increased vascular per-
meability, bronchoconstriction, and cardiovascular collapse.

2.3 Pathophysiological Progression
The progression of anaphylaxis follows a characteristic timeline:
1. Exposure (T=0): Allergen cross-links IgE on mast cells
2. Early Phase (T=0-5 min): Mast cell degranulation →histamine, tryptase release
3. Progressive Phase (T=5-15 min): Cytokine cascade, leukotriene release, PAF activation
4. Critical Phase (T=15-30 min): Vasodilation, bronchoconstriction, hypotension, shock
5. Biphasic Reaction (T=4-12 hr): Recurrence without re-exposure in 20% of cases

2.5 Current Diagnostic Challenges
• No real-time biomarker test exists for acute anaphylaxis
• Serum tryptase peaks at 60-90 minutes — too late for early intervention
• Clinical diagnosis relies on visible symptoms, which patients may not recognize
• Subjective assessment causes delays in epinephrine administration
• Children and anxious patients cannot reliably communicate symptoms
3. CURRENT HOSPITAL HANDLING AND PROBLEMS
3.1 Standard Hospital Protocol for Anaphylaxis
ABCDE Approach:
1. Airway: Assess patency, prepare for intubation if angioedema present
2. Breathing: Oxygen therapy, bronchodilators for bronchospasm
3. Circulation: IV access, fluid resuscitation (1-2L crystalloid)
Generated by Kimi.ai

4. Disability: Neurological assessment
5. Exposure: Remove trigger, examine for urticaria/angioedema
Primary Treatment:
• Epinephrine IM (0.3-0.5 mg of 1:1000) into anterolateral thigh
• Repeat every 5-10 minutes as needed
• IV epinephrine infusion for refractory cases
• Adjuncts: Antihistamines, corticosteroids, bronchodilators

3.3 Key Statistics on Treatment Failures
• 50% of patients presenting to ED with anaphylaxis do NOT receive epinephrine
• Death from anaphylaxis still occurs despite treatability — primarily due to delayed recognition
• Biphasic reactions occur in 20% of cases, often missed during short observation
• Refractory anaphylaxis requires prolonged critical care support (hours to days)
3.4 Gaps in Current Technology
1. No wearable device provides continuous multi-parameter physiological monitoring for anaphylaxis
2. Existing auto-injectors require manual activation by patient/caregiver
3. No AI-driven early warning system exists for pre-symptomatic detection
4. Lack of integration between wearable monitoring and hospital EMR systems
5. No automated emergency response chain for severe reactions

4. PROPOSED SOLUTION
4.1 System Overview
The Intelligent Physiological Pattern-Based System is a wearable IoT medical device that:
1. Continuously monitors multi-modal physiological signals (PPG, temperature, EDA, accelerom-
eter, respiratory)
2. Intelligently analyzes patterns using ensemble machine learning models (LSTM, Random Forest,
SVM)
3. Detects anaphylaxis early — before visible symptoms become severe
4. Automatically intervenes through a tiered response system
5. Integrates with hospital EMR and emergency services

6. WORKING OF EACH COMPONENT
6.1 PPG Sensor (MAX30102)
Function: Measures photoplethysmography signals for heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), and
heart rate variability (HRV).
Working Principle:
Generated by Kimi.ai

• Uses red (660nm) and infrared (880nm) LEDs with photodetector
• Light absorption varies with blood volume changes in capillaries
• AC component = pulsatile arterial blood; DC component = venous blood + tissue
• SpO2 calculated from ratio of ratios: R = (AC_red/DC_red) / (AC_ir/DC_ir)
• HRV derived from inter-beat intervals (IBI) in PPG peaks
Anaphylaxis Relevance:
• Tachycardia is one of the earliest cardiovascular signs
• HRV decreases significantly due to sympathetic activation
• SpO2 drops during respiratory compromise
Interface: I2C protocol with ESP32-S3
6.2 Temperature Sensor (MLX90614)
Function: Non-contact infrared measurement of skin temperature.
Working Principle:
• Infrared thermopile detects thermal radiation from skin
• Integrated DSP calculates temperature from sensor voltage
• Factory-calibrated with 0.5°C accuracy
Anaphylaxis Relevance:
• Early flushing causes 0.5-1.5°C skin temperature rise
• Late phase: profuse sweating causes temperature drop
• Pattern of rise-then-fall is characteristic of anaphylaxis progression
Interface: I2C protocol with ESP32-S3
6.3 EDA/GSR Sensor
Function: Measures electrodermal activity (skin conductance) as indicator of sympathetic nervous sys-
tem activation.
Working Principle:
• Applies small constant voltage (0.5V) across two electrodes
• Measures conductance changes due to sweat gland activity
• Tonic (SCL) and phasic (SCR) components separated
Anaphylaxis Relevance:
• Sympathetic activation causes immediate increase in skin conductance
• One of the earliest measurable physiological changes
• Correlates with histamine release and mast cell activation
Interface: Analog input to ESP32-S3 ADC (12-bit resolution)
Generated by Kimi.ai

6.4 IMU (MPU6050)
Function: 6-axis motion tracking (3-axis accelerometer + 3-axis gyroscope).
Working Principle:
• MEMS-based capacitive sensing for acceleration and rotation
• Detects patient posture, movement patterns, and falls
• DMP (Digital Motion Processor) offloads computation from main MCU
Anaphylaxis Relevance:
• Detects sudden collapse or loss of consciousness
• Monitors restlessness/agitation in early phase
• Fall detection triggers immediate emergency alert
Interface: I2C protocol with ESP32-S3
6.5 ESP32-S3 Microcontroller
Function: Central processing unit for data acquisition, preprocessing, edge AI inference, and communi-
cation.
Key Specifications:
• Dual-core Xtensa LX7 @ 240MHz
• 512KB SRAM + 8MB PSRAM
• Wi-Fi 4 (802.11 b/g/n) + BLE 5.0
• Ultra-low power coprocessor (ULP)
• Hardware floating-point unit (FPU)
• Rich peripheral interface: 45 GPIO, 4 SPI, 2 I2C, 2 I2S, 3 UART
Firmware Modules:
1. Sensor Acquisition Task (Core 0): Reads all sensors at configured sampling rates
2. Signal Processing Task (Core 0): Applies filters, removes artifacts
3. Feature Extraction Task (Core 1): Computes HRV, statistical features
4. Inference Task (Core 1): Runs quantized LSTM model (TensorFlow Lite Micro)
5. Communication Task (Core 0): MQTT publish/subscribe, WiFi management
6. Alert Task (Core 1): Manages buzzer, vibration, auto-injector trigger
6.6 Signal Processing Module
Digital Filtering:
• PPG: Bandpass filter (0.5-8 Hz) to remove baseline wander and high-frequency noise
• EDA: Low-pass filter (0.05-5 Hz) to isolate relevant conductance changes
• Accelerometer: High-pass filter (>0.5 Hz) to remove gravity component
Generated by Kimi.ai

Artifact Removal:
• Adaptive thresholding for motion artifact detection
• Wavelet denoising for PPG signal enhancement
• Outlier rejection using Z-score method
Signal Segmentation:
• Sliding window approach: 30-second windows with 50% overlap
• Each window generates a feature vector of 45 dimensions
6.7 Feature Extraction Engine
Time-Domain Features:
• Mean, Standard Deviation, RMS, Skewness, Kurtosis
• Peak-to-peak amplitude, Zero-crossing rate
Frequency-Domain Features:
• Power Spectral Density (PSD) using Welch’s method
• Low Frequency (LF: 0.04-0.15 Hz) and High Frequency (HF: 0.15-0.4 Hz) power
• LF/HF ratio (sympathovagal balance)
HRV Features (from PPG):
• RMSSD (Root Mean Square of Successive Differences)
• pNN50 (percentage of successive NN intervals >50ms)
• SDNN (Standard Deviation of NN intervals)
• SDSD (Standard Deviation of Successive Differences)
Non-Linear Features:
• Sample Entropy (complexity measure)
• Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (DFA) ￿1 and ￿2
• Poincaré plot SD1 and SD2
Multi-Parameter Fusion:
• Concatenated feature vector:
[PPG_features, Temp_features, EDA_features, IMU_features,
Resp_features]
• Total dimensionality: ~120 features per window
6.8 Ensemble ML Model
Architecture:
Input Layer (120 features)
│
├──→LSTM Branch (Temporal patterns)
│
LSTM-128 →Dropout(0.3) →LSTM-64 →Dense-32
Generated by Kimi.ai

│
├──→Random Forest Branch (Static patterns)
│
200 estimators, max_depth=15, gini criterion
│
├──→SVM Branch (Boundary detection)
│
RBF kernel, C=1.0, gamma='scale'
│
└──→Voting Classifier (Soft voting)
Weighted average: LSTM(0.5) + RF(0.3) + SVM(0.2)
Output: Anaphylaxis Probability (0-1)
Training Pipeline:
1. Data Collection: Simulated anaphylaxis data + public datasets (MIMIC-III, PhysioNet)
2. Data Augmentation: SMOTE for class imbalance, Gaussian noise injection
3. Cross-Validation: 5-fold stratified CV
4. Hyperparameter Tuning: Bayesian optimization (Optuna)
5. Quantization: Post-training INT8 quantization for edge deployment
Performance Targets:
• Sensitivity: >95% (minimize false negatives)
• Specificity: >90% (minimize false positives)
• Latency: <50ms (edge inference)
• AUC-ROC: >0.95
6.9 Auto-Injector Actuator
Mechanism:
• Spring-loaded epinephrine cartridge (0.3mg, 1:1000 concentration)
• Servo motor releases safety lock upon ML trigger
• Needle penetration depth: 10-15mm (IM injection into anterolateral thigh)
• Mechanical override button for manual activation
• Safety interlock prevents accidental discharge
Safety Features:
• Double-confirmation: ML model + secondary threshold check
• Patient cancellation window: 10-second countdown with audible warning
• Tamper-evident cartridge seal
• Temperature monitoring (epinephrine degrades >25°C)
6.10 Cloud Backend
Data Flow:
Generated by Kimi.ai

1. ESP32 publishes sensor data to MQTT topics every 1 second
2. MQTT broker (HiveMQ) routes data to subscribers
3. Kafka streams data to InfluxDB (time-series storage)
4. ML pipeline retrains models weekly with new data
5. Alert service triggers notifications based on severity
API Endpoints:
• POST /api/v1/data/ingest — Sensor data ingestion
• GET /api/v1/patients/{id}/vitals — Real-time vital signs
• GET /api/v1/patients/{id}/history — Historical data
• POST /api/v1/alerts — Alert management
• GET /api/v1/models/status — Model performance metrics

Key Findings:
• Incidence: 2.1 per 1,000 person-years in the US
• Most reactions occur OUTSIDE hospital settings
• Only ~50% of ED patients meeting anaphylaxis criteria receive epinephrine
• Delayed epinephrine administration is associated with worse outcomes and mortality
• Reasons for failure: delayed presentation, misdiagnosis as mild reaction, failure to use NIAID/

Relevance to Project:
• Validates the need for pre-hospital detection and intervention
• Confirms that current diagnostic methods are insuﬀicient

Key Findings:
